| Strategy | URLs | Best for | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Cookie` (default) | `/about` | Apps behind a login | Prerendered pages hold the default language and switch on load, so others can flash briefly, and search engines mostly see one language |
| `UrlPrefix` | `/de/about` | Public sites and SEO | Every language gets its own prerendered pages. Plain paths redirect to the visitor's language. Links must use `localizeHref`, or pages won't be prerendered per language |

On the server, `call.svelteLocale` and `call.messages` follow the same rules: the URL prefix if that strategy is on, then the cookie, then `Accept-Language`, then your default. `localizeHref` is safe with either strategy.

Parameters are plain text replacements. Plurals and date formatting aren't built in yet.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security

# Security

The protections that are on by default, and how to change them.

## Security headers

Security headers are on by default. Every response gets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. Each is a property you can change, or set to `null` to leave out:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    securityHeaders {
        referrerPolicy = "no-referrer"
    }
}
```

Every HTML page from your build also gets a strict `Content-Security-Policy`:

```
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-...'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none';
base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
```

`script-src` lists the SHA-256 hash of each inline `<script>` in that page, which covers SvelteKit's startup script and the theme and locale script ktor-svelte adds, and nothing else. `svelteBundle` computes these hashes at build time and stores them in the manifest, so the server never reads a page to build its policy. For builds without them, such as a directory build in development, the server hashes each page once and caches the result. Other inline scripts and scripts from other origins are blocked. The other directives exist for these reasons:

- `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`: Svelte transitions and many components set inline styles, and SvelteKit can inline small CSS files.
- `img-src` and `font-src` allow `data:` because Tailwind, DaisyUI and Vite inline small images, icons and fonts as data URLs. `blob:` covers images made in the browser, such as upload previews.
- `frame-ancestors` follows `frameOptions`: `'none'` for `DENY`, `'self'` for `SAMEORIGIN`, and left out when `frameOptions` is `null`.

API responses, JavaScript, CSS and other files get no CSP, since it only matters for documents.

To load something from another origin, such as an analytics script, add sources to a directive. A directive that is not in the policy yet is added with exactly the sources you list:

```kotlin
securityHeaders {
    allowCspSources("script-src", "https://plausible.io")
    allowCspSources("connect-src", "https://plausible.io")
    allowCspSources("img-src", "https://avatars.example.com")
}
```

To use your own policy instead, set `contentSecurityPolicy`. It is then sent unchanged on every response, and `allowCspSources` is ignored. Inline scripts in your pages break unless your policy allows them, for example with SvelteKit's own `csp` option in `hash` mode.

To opt out:

```kotlin
securityHeaders { automaticContentSecurityPolicy = false }
securityHeaders { enabled = false }
```

The first turns off only the automatic CSP. The second turns off all security headers.

No CSP is sent while the dev proxy is active, because Vite injects its own scripts. The other headers are still sent.

## API request guards

Two checks protect every path under your API prefixes. Both are on by default.

**Origin check.** POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and every other method except GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE from a browser on another site are refused with 403, so a cookie session cannot be used for cross-site request forgery. A request is refused when:

- its `Origin` header names a different host than the request, or is `null`, or
- it has no `Origin` but sends `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`.

Only the host is compared, ignoring case, scheme and port, so a TLS-terminating proxy or the Vite dev port does not cause false rejections. The request host comes from Ktor's `origin`, so it follows `XForwardedHeaders` or `ForwardedHeaders` when you install them. Requests with neither header, such as curl, server-to-server calls and tests, are allowed, because browsers always send one of them. GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE are never checked.

To accept writes from another frontend, such as a separate admin app, list its exact origin:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    allowedOrigins("https://admin.example.com")
}
```

**Body size limit.** Request bodies on API paths are limited to 1 MiB. Larger bodies get 413, whether they send `Content-Length` or are chunked. It uses Ktor's `RequestBodyLimit` plugin, so do not install that plugin yourself unless you set `maxApiBodySize = null`.

A refused cross-origin write gets `{"message":"Cross-origin API request refused."}`. In development mode the message also says how to allow the origin, which production leaves out so it does not tell attackers which setting to look for. Other refused requests get a JSON body such as `{"message":"Request body is larger than the limit of 1048576 bytes."}`.

**Error details.** In production, an exception that no route handles answers with its status and a generic message, such as `{"message":"Internal Server Error."}` on API paths, instead of the exception message, which Ktor sends by default and which can reveal internals. Malformed or unreadable bodies keep their 400 or 415 without naming your classes. The exception is still logged. In development mode, or when you install `StatusPages`, nothing changes. Set `hideErrorDetails = false` to send the messages again.

To raise the limit, or turn the origin check off:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    originCheck = false
    maxApiBodySize = 10L * 1024 * 1024
}
```

Set `maxApiBodySize = null` to remove the limit.

Paths outside your API prefixes, such as frontend files and the dev proxy, are not affected.

**Counting refusals.** ktor-svelte counts every refused request, so attacks and misconfigurations show up as numbers, not only as log lines. Read the counters from `application.svelteMetrics`, or from the `refusals` object of the status endpoint. To export them, bind them to your metrics library, for example Micrometer:

```kotlin
val metrics = svelteMetrics
registry.gauge("svelte.refusals", listOf(Tag.of("reason", "cross_origin")), metrics) { it.crossOriginRefusals.toDouble() }
registry.gauge("svelte.refusals", listOf(Tag.of("reason", "body_too_large")), metrics) { it.bodyTooLargeRefusals.toDouble() }
registry.gauge("svelte.refusals", listOf(Tag.of("reason", "rate_limit")), metrics) { it.rateLimitRefusals.toDouble() }
```

**JSON shape.** A small body can still be expensive to parse when it nests thousands of arrays. JSON bodies on API paths are checked while they stream in, before any parsing: more than 64 levels of nesting answers 400 with `{"message":"Request JSON is nested deeper than 64 levels."}`. Set `maxJsonStringLength` to also refuse long strings, which is off by default because the body limit already caps them:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    maxJsonDepth = 32
    maxJsonStringLength = 10_000
}
```

Set `maxJsonDepth = null` to turn the depth check off.

**Rate limit.** Each client may send 120 writes per minute to your API paths, meaning every method except GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE. More get 429 with a `Retry-After` header. Reads and frontend files are never limited. Clients are told apart by `call.request.origin.remoteHost`, so behind a reverse proxy install `XForwardedHeaders` or `ForwardedHeaders`, or every user shares one limit.

Routes such as login need a much tighter limit. Name one, and wrap the routes in Ktor's own `rateLimit`:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    rateLimit {
        apiWrites = 300
        limit("login", requests = 5, per = 1.minutes)
    }
}

routing {
    rateLimit(RateLimitName("login")) {
        post("/api/login") { /* ... */ }
    }
}
```

Limits use a fixed window by default: the budget refills completely at the end of each period, so a client can send a full budget just before the edge and another just after it. Pick another algorithm when that matters:

| Algorithm | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `RateLimitAlgorithm.FixedWindow` | The default. Cheapest, but allows a burst of twice the limit around the window edge |
| `RateLimitAlgorithm.SlidingWindow` | Never more than the limit in any period, wherever it starts |
| `RateLimitAlgorithm.TokenBucket` | Allows a burst up to the limit, then refills steadily over the period |

```kotlin
rateLimit {
    algorithm = RateLimitAlgorithm.SlidingWindow
    limit("login", requests = 5, per = 1.minutes, algorithm = RateLimitAlgorithm.TokenBucket)
}
```

By default every client address gets its own budget. Choose another key when that is wrong, for example many users behind one office address. `key` applies to every limit, and a named limit can take its own:

```kotlin
rateLimit {
    key { call -> call.sessions.get<UserSession>()?.userId ?: call.request.origin.remoteHost }
    limit("export", requests = 2, per = 1.hours) { call -> call.sessions.get<UserSession>()?.userId ?: "anonymous" }
}
```

The default limit runs before routing, so read the user from the session there, not from `call.principal()`, which only `authenticate` routes set. Do not read the request body in a key: it would be gone by the time your route receives it.

It uses Ktor's `RateLimit` plugin, so do not install that plugin yourself unless you set `rateLimit { enabled = false }`. `apiWrites = 0` keeps the named limits but drops the default one.

## Software bill of materials

Every [GitHub release](https://github.com/nijasc/ktor-svelte/releases) has a [CycloneDX](https://cyclonedx.org) SBOM for each artifact attached: `ktor-svelte-server-<version>.cdx.json` and `ktor-svelte-gradle-plugin-<version>.cdx.json`. They list the runtime dependencies with versions, licenses and hashes, so you can feed them to Dependency-Track or a license scanner before approving an upgrade. Test and compile-only dependencies are left out. The plugin's own list is short, because Gradle provides the rest.

## Verifying a release

Every JAR of a release, for the runtime and for the Gradle plugin, has signed [SLSA build provenance](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.0/provenance). It records that the file was built by the release workflow of this repository from the tagged commit, and it is signed with [Sigstore](https://www.sigstore.dev) through GitHub artifact attestations. To check a JAR you downloaded, for example from Maven Central or your Gradle cache, use the GitHub CLI:

```bash
gh attestation verify ktor-svelte-server-<version>.jar --repo nijasc/ktor-svelte
```

It fails if the file was changed or built anywhere else. Maven Central also has the usual PGP signature next to every file.

## Reporting a vulnerability

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/nijasc/ktor-svelte/blob/main/SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability privately, and for a table of every secure default.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/

# Recipes

Short, complete answers to tasks most apps need. Each one uses only Ktor, SvelteKit and what ktor-svelte already does, so you can copy it and adapt the names.

- [Sign in with a session cookie](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/sessions)
- [Upload files](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/uploads)
- [Stream live updates](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/live-updates)
- [Page through long lists](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/pagination)
- [Add an admin area](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/admin-area)

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/sessions

# Sign in with a session cookie

The frontend and the API share one origin, so a plain cookie is all you need: no tokens in `localStorage`, no CORS. The origin check that ktor-svelte turns on refuses cross-site writes, which protects the cookie from cross-site request forgery.

Add `ktor-server-auth` and `ktor-server-sessions`, then:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class UserSession(val userId: String)

fun Application.sessionAuth(users: Users) {
    install(Sessions) {
        cookie<UserSession>("session") {
            cookie.path = "/"
            cookie.httpOnly = true
            cookie.secure = !this@sessionAuth.developmentMode
            cookie.extensions["SameSite"] = "Lax"
            transform(SessionTransportTransformerMessageAuthentication(hex(System.getenv("SESSION_SIGN_KEY"))))
        }
    }
    install(Authentication) {
        session<UserSession>("session") {
            validate { session -> session }
            challenge { call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, Problem("Sign in first.")) }
        }
    }
    install(Svelte) {
        rateLimit { limit("login", requests = 5, per = 1.minutes) }
        errorResponse<Problem>(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized)
    }
    routing {
        rateLimit(RateLimitName("login")) {
            post("/api/session") {
                val login = call.receive<Login>()
                val user = users.check(login.email, login.password)
                if (user == null) return@post call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, Problem("Wrong email or password."))
                call.sessions.set(UserSession(user.id))
                call.respond(user)
            }
        }
        delete("/api/session") {
            call.sessions.clear<UserSession>()
            call.respond(HttpStatusCode.NoContent)
        }
        authenticate("session") {
            get("/api/me") {
                val user: User? = users.find(call.principal<UserSession>()!!.userId)
                if (user == null) call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, Problem("Sign in first.")) else call.respond(user)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

- `SESSION_SIGN_KEY` is a long random hex string. Generate it once per environment and keep it out of the repository.
- The `login` limit allows five attempts per minute and client, on top of the default limit for all API writes.
- `errorResponse` adds the 401 to the typed errors of every endpoint, because `authenticate` answers it outside your route.

In the frontend, send users to the login page whenever the API says they are signed out:

```ts
import { goto } from '$app/navigation';
import { api, apiConfig, isApiError } from '#api';

apiConfig.onUnauthorized = () => goto('/login');

try {
    const user = await api.session.create({ email, password });
} catch (error) {
    if (isApiError(error, 'session.create')) message = error.body.message;
    else throw error;
}
```

Put the `onUnauthorized` line in your root `+layout.ts`, so it runs once in the browser.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/uploads

# Upload files

Receive the parts in Ktor and describe the body once, so the generated function takes `FormData`:

```kotlin
post("/api/files") {
    val stored = mutableListOf<StoredFile>()
    call.receiveMultipart().forEachPart { part ->
        if (part is PartData.FileItem) {
            stored += files.store(part.originalFileName ?: "upload", part.provider().readRemaining().readByteArray())
        }
        part.dispose()
    }
    call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Created, stored)
}.describe {
    requestBody { ContentType.MultiPart.FormData() }
}
```

```ts
const form = new FormData();
for (const file of input.files ?? []) form.append('file', file);
const stored = await api.files.create(form, {
    onUploadProgress: ({ loaded, total }) => (progress = total ? loaded / total : 0)
});
```

- API bodies are limited to 1 MiB by default. Raise `maxApiBodySize` to the largest upload you accept.
- `readRemaining()` keeps each file in memory. For large files, copy `part.provider()` to a file or object storage instead.
- Never use `originalFileName` as a path on disk. Store files under an ID you choose.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/live-updates

# Stream live updates

Server-sent events need no extra client library, and the generated client turns them into an async generator:

```kotlin
install(SSE)
routing {
    sse("/api/ticks") {
        repeat(10) { count ->
            send(ServerSentEvent(Json.encodeToString(Tick(count))))
            delay(1000)
        }
    }.describe {
        responses {
            HttpStatusCode.OK {
                ContentType.Text.EventStream { schema = jsonSchema<Tick>() }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
    import { api, type Tick } from '#api';

    let ticks = $state<Tick[]>([]);

    $effect(() => {
        const controller = new AbortController();
        (async () => {
            for await (const tick of api.ticks.list({ signal: controller.signal })) ticks.push(tick);
        })().catch(() => undefined);
        return () => controller.abort();
    });
</script>
```

- The `describe` block gives the events a type. Without it, each event is a string.
- Aborting the signal when the component goes away closes the connection.
- SSE counts as a GET, so it is never rate limited or blocked by the origin check.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/pagination

# Page through long lists

Return `Page<T>` with a `cursor` query parameter, and `pages` reads it one page at a time:

```kotlin
get("/api/users") {
    val cursor = call.queryParameters["cursor"]
    val limit = call.queryParameters["limit"]?.toIntOrNull() ?: 50
    val page: Page<User> = users.page(cursor, limit.coerceIn(1, 100))
    call.respond(page)
}
```

```ts
import { api, pages } from '#api';

for await (const users of pages(api.users.list, { limit: '100' })) table.push(...users);
```

- Use the ID or sort key of the last item as the cursor, not an offset, so rows added while someone pages do not shift the results.
- Always cap `limit` on the server.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/recipes/admin-area

# Add an admin area

Protect the API on the server and only hide the pages in the frontend. A page guard alone protects nothing, because anyone can call the API directly.

```kotlin
fun Route.admin(
    users: Users,
    build: Route.() -> Unit,
) {
    authenticate("session") {
        route("/api/admin") {
            install(
                createRouteScopedPlugin("AdminOnly") {
                    onCall { call ->
                        val user = call.principal<UserSession>()?.let { users.find(it.userId) }
                        if (user?.admin != true) call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Forbidden, Problem("Admins only."))
                    }
                },
            )
            build()
        }
    }
}

routing {
    admin(users) {
        get("/users") { call.respond(users.all()) }
    }
}
```

In SvelteKit, put the admin pages under `src/routes/admin/` and check the user once in their layout:

```ts
import { redirect } from '@sveltejs/kit';
import { apiWith } from '#api';
import type { LayoutLoad } from './$types';

export const ssr = false;

export const load: LayoutLoad = async (event) => {
    const me = await apiWith(event).me.list().catch(() => undefined);
    if (!me?.admin) redirect(307, '/login');
    return { me };
};
```

Pages inside it call `api.admin.getUsers()` and the other admin endpoints. Every one of them answers 403 for anyone who is not an admin, whatever the frontend shows.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/ktor

# Ktor settings

Every setting of `install(Svelte) { }`.

The values shown are the defaults.

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    apiPrefixes("/api")
    paramRoutes()
    spaFallback = "200.html"
    notFoundPage = "404.html"
    source = SvelteSource.Classpath
    generateTs = false
    generateTsOutput = null
    apiDocs = false
    apiDocsPath = "/api/docs"
    routing = SvelteRouting.Automatic
    originCheck = true
    hideErrorDetails = true
    apiCompression = true
    allowedOrigins()
    maxApiBodySize = 1048576
    maxJsonDepth = 64
    maxJsonStringLength = null
    sitemap = true
    defaultFavicon = true
    siteUrl = null

    securityHeaders {
        enabled = true
        contentTypeOptions = "nosniff"
        frameOptions = "DENY"
        referrerPolicy = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
        contentSecurityPolicy = null
        automaticContentSecurityPolicy = true
    }

    cache {
        immutable = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
        html = "no-cache"
        other = "no-cache"
    }

    dev {
        url = "http://localhost:5173"
        mode = DevMode.AUTO
        allowRemote = false
        panel = true
        browserLogs = true
    }

    transport {
    }
}
```

| Setting | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `apiPrefixes` | Paths the frontend never answers, and the routes included in `generateTs`. `/api` matches `/api` and `/api/x`, not `/apiary` |
| `paramRoutes` | SvelteKit route patterns such as `/items/[id]`, `/docs/[...rest]` and `/blog/[[page]]`. Matching paths get the fallback even when the request does not accept HTML, for example link previews or tests. Paths with a file extension still return 404 |
| `spaFallback` | Page for client-side routes. Must match the adapter's `fallback` option. `null` disables it |
| `notFoundPage` | Page served with status 404. `null` disables it |
| `source` | `SvelteSource.Classpath`, or `SvelteSource.Directory(path)` to serve a build from disk |
| `generateTs` | Generates TypeScript from your routes in development mode |
| `generateTsOutput` | Output directory. Defaults to `src/lib/api` in your frontend |
| `apiDocs` | Serves Swagger UI in development mode. See [API docs](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#api-docs) |
| `routing` | `Manual` lets you place the frontend with `svelte()`. See [Auth](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/auth) |
| `originCheck` | Refuses cross-site requests to API paths for every method except GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE. See [API request guards](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards) |
| `buildHeader` | Sends the frontend build fingerprint on API responses as `X-Ktor-Svelte-Build`, so the client can notice a deploy. On by default |
| `maxJsonDepth` | Refuses JSON request bodies on API paths that nest deeper than this, with 400. `64` by default, `null` turns it off |
| `maxJsonStringLength` | Refuses JSON request bodies on API paths with a longer string, with 400. Off by default |
| `sitemap` | Serves a generated `/sitemap.xml` and `/robots.txt` when the build has none. On by default. See [Sitemap and robots.txt](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#sitemap-and-robots-txt) |
| `siteUrl` | Public address used in the sitemap, such as `https://example.com`. `null` takes it from the request |
| `defaultFavicon` | Serves a ktor-svelte favicon while the app has none of its own. On by default. See [Default favicon](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#default-favicon) |
| `requestIds` | Gives every request an `X-Request-Id`, keeps one sent by the client and logs it with unhandled errors. On by default |
| `hideErrorDetails` | Answers unhandled exceptions in production without their message. See [API request guards](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards) |
| `apiCompression` | Compresses API responses of 1 KiB or more with gzip, deflate or zstd. On by default. See [API compression](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/transport#api-compression) |
| `allowedOrigins` | Extra origins, such as `https://admin.example.com`, that may write to the API |
| `maxApiBodySize` | Largest request body on API paths, in bytes. `null` disables it |
| `securityHeaders.enabled` | Sends security headers. `false` turns all of them off. See [Security headers](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#security-headers) |
| `securityHeaders.contentSecurityPolicy` | Your own policy, sent unchanged on every response. `null` uses the automatic policy |
| `securityHeaders.automaticContentSecurityPolicy` | Sends a strict CSP built from the inline scripts of each HTML page. Extend it with `allowCspSources(directive, sources)` |
| `publicConfig(value)` | Values for the frontend. `publicConfig { ... }` reads them again on every request in development. See [Runtime config](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/runtime-config) |
| `cache` | `Cache-Control` values for `_app/immutable/**`, HTML pages and other files |
| `dev.url` | Vite URL. The `KTOR_SVELTE_DEV_SERVER` environment variable overrides it |
| `dev.mode` | `AUTO` follows Ktor's development mode. `ALWAYS` and `NEVER` force it |
| `dev.allowRemote` | Lets other machines use the dev proxy, and lets `dev.url` point at another machine. Off by default |
| `dev.browserLogs` | Sends browser console output, uncaught errors and unhandled rejections from pages proxied from Vite to the app's log. On by default |
| `dev.panel` | Shows a panel of recent API calls, with status, timing and validation errors, on pages proxied from Vite. On by default. See [Dev workflow](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/guide/dev-workflow) |
| `transport` | JSON, XML and compression. See [Transport](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/transport) |

A route of yours such as `get("/{slug}")` beats the frontend. That is intended, but it can hide pages.

ETags are content hashes from the manifest, so 304 responses are cheap and stay valid across restarts. If you set `adapter({ precompress: true })`, the `.br` and `.gz` files are served based on `Accept-Encoding`. Files the adapter did not compress, such as those from `static/`, are gzipped by `svelteBundle` unless you set `precompress = false`. `.zst` files next to them, for example from a Vite compression plugin, are bundled too and preferred for browsers that accept `zstd`, since they decompress faster.

If the frontend build is missing, the app fails at startup in production with a message explaining what to do. In Ktor development mode it logs a warning instead, and frontend routes return a 503 explaining the problem.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/gradle

# Gradle settings and tasks

Every setting of `svelte { }`, every task and every Gradle property.

The values shown are the defaults.

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktor.svelte.gradle.PackageManager

svelte {
    frontendDir = layout.projectDirectory.dir("frontend")
    outputDir = "build"
    packageManager = PackageManager.AUTO
    buildScript = "build"
    buildEnv = emptySet()
    addRuntimeDependency = true
    includeSourceMaps = false
    precompress = true
    dev {
        port = 5173
        script = "dev"
        debugPort = 5005
        openBrowser = true
    }
}
```

| Setting | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `frontendDir` | Directory of the SvelteKit project |
| `outputDir` | Adapter output, a folder inside `frontendDir` given relative to it. Must match the adapter's `pages` option |
| `packageManager` | `AUTO`, `BUN`, `PNPM`, `NPM` or `YARN`. `AUTO` picks from `bun.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock` |
| `bunVersion` | An exact Bun version, such as `"1.3.14"`, that ktor-svelte downloads and uses instead of the Bun on `PATH`. Unset by default. See [Pin Bun](#pin-bun) |
| `buildScript` | `package.json` script that builds the frontend |
| `buildEnv` | Environment variables that affect the build. Declare any your frontend reads through `$env`, or Gradle can reuse a stale build |
| `libraries` | Tailwind, DaisyUI, Lucide and i18n. See [Frontend libraries](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/frontend-libraries) |
| `addRuntimeDependency` | Adds `ktor-svelte-server` to `implementation`, at the plugin's own version |
| `includeSourceMaps` | Ships `.map` files in the JAR, where anyone can download them. Off by default |
| `precompress` | Gzips text files of 1 KiB or more that have no `.br` or `.gz` variant yet, such as SVG, JSON and fonts from `static/`, and keeps the result only when it saves at least 10%. On by default |
| `dev.port` | Port passed to Vite by `svelteDev` |
| `dev.script` | `package.json` script that starts Vite |
| `dev.debugPort` | Port where the app started by `svelteDevAll` listens for a debugger, on `127.0.0.1` only. `0` turns it off |
| `dev.openBrowser` | Opens the app in the default browser once `svelteDevAll` is ready, the first time only. Never in CI or without a display |

The package manager must already be installed unless you set `bunVersion`. The plugin does not download Node.

In a Groovy `build.gradle`, a misspelled setting such as `fronendDir = file('web')` fails with the closest name and the list of settings, instead of Gradle's generic missing property error. The Kotlin DSL catches the same mistake when it compiles the script.

## Review your configuration

`./gradlew svelteConfig` gives an overview of how ktor-svelte is set up in your app. It lists the Gradle settings, then starts your app once to read the effective `install(Svelte) { }` settings, the same way `svelteGenerateTs` does, so it shows what really runs, including values set from environment variables. Settings you changed are marked with their default, which makes it easy to see what a new version changed or added after an upgrade.

Then it scores the setup and lists what to change:

```text
Scores
  Security              [#########-]  90%  10 of 11
  Performance           [##########] 100%  4 of 4
  Operations            [#######---]  66%  2 of 3
  Developer experience  [##########] 100%  4 of 4

Suggestions
  - [Security] Set maxJsonStringLength = 100_000, or the longest text your API accepts.
  - [Operations] Set healthEndpoint = true and point your orchestrator at /_ktor-svelte/health.
```

The checks cover the origin check, security headers and CSP, error details, body and JSON limits, rate limits, the dev proxy, source maps, compression, caching, health and request IDs, generated TypeScript and dev tooling. A suggestion is advice, not an error: a public API may well do without `healthEndpoint`. Without the `application` plugin, only the Gradle settings are shown.

## Pin Bun

A fresh CI image or laptop often has no package manager, so the first build fails. Set `bunVersion` and the plugin downloads that exact Bun from Bun's GitHub releases the first time a task needs it:

```kotlin
svelte {
    bunVersion = "1.3.14"
}
```

The archive is checked against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt` before it is unpacked into `~/.gradle/ktor-svelte/bun/<version>/`, and every later build reuses it. Every task then uses this Bun, even when another one is on `PATH`, so all machines build with the same version. With `packageManager = AUTO`, Bun becomes the package manager. Bun runs Vite itself, so Node is not needed. It works on Windows, macOS and Linux, including Alpine, on x64 and arm64. Behind a proxy, set Java's `https.proxyHost` and `https.proxyPort` in `gradle.properties` with the `systemProp.` prefix.

## Gradle tasks

| Task | What it does |
|---|---|
| `svelteSync` | Installs configured libraries and writes their generated files |
| `svelteVerifySync` | Fails if libraries don't match your config. Runs before every frontend build |
| `svelteGenerateSources` | Generates Kotlin for your libraries. Runs before compiling |
| `svelteInit` | Creates a working SvelteKit project in an empty `frontendDir`. Takes `--package-manager=bun` |
| `svelteDoctor` | Checks adapter, adapter output against `svelte.outputDir`, the bundled manifest, `#api`, tsconfig, Kit version, Node, tool and port, and says what to fix |
| `svelteConfig` | Prints every setting of `svelte { }` and of `install(Svelte) { }`, marks the ones you changed from the default, scores security, performance, operations and developer experience, and suggests what to turn on. See [Review your configuration](#review-your-configuration) |
| `svelteDevAll` | Runs Vite, the Kotlin compiler and your app, and restarts the app when Kotlin changes |
| `svelteDev` | Starts Vite |
| `svelteGenerateTs` | Starts your app once to regenerate TypeScript |
| `svelteVerifyTs` | Starts your app once and fails if the committed TypeScript is out of date. Runs as part of `check` |
| `svelteCheck` | Runs your `check` script |
| `svelteRun --script=lint` | Runs any `package.json` script. Pass arguments with `--args="--fix --quiet"`; quote an argument that contains spaces |
| `svelteOutdated` | Lists outdated frontend dependencies |
| `svelteUpdateDependencies` | Updates frontend dependencies and the lockfile |
| `svelteClean` | Deletes `node_modules`, `.svelte-kit` and the build output |
| `deepClean` | Runs `clean`, then also deletes the project's `.gradle` and `.kotlin` directories, `node_modules`, `.svelte-kit`, `.vite`, `.turbo`, `.cache`, `.eslintcache` and the build output. Lockfiles and generated files are kept. Files a running Gradle daemon or IDE still holds, which happens on Windows, are skipped with a warning |
| `svelteLiveTemplates` | Writes IntelliJ live templates to `build/ktor-svelte/live-templates/`. `--install` copies them into every IntelliJ IDEA and WebStorm configuration it finds, `--config-dir=...` picks another JetBrains folder |
| `svelteGenerateRunConfigurations` | Writes IntelliJ run configurations to `.run/`, keeping any that exist |

| Property | Effect |
|---|---|
| `-Psvelte.skip=true` | Skips the frontend build, and warns if a JAR is being built |
| `-Psvelte.dev=true` | Same as skip, and also sets `-Dio.ktor.development=true` on `run` |
| `-Psvelte.verifyTs=false` | Leaves `svelteVerifyTs` out of `check` |
| `-Psvelte.verbose=true` | Shows the package manager and Vite output of `svelteInstall`, `svelteBuild`, `svelteSync` and `svelteInit`. Without it, that output is hidden when the command succeeds and printed in full when it fails. `--info` also shows it |

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/how-it-works

# How it works

What happens at build time and how each request is answered.

At build time, three tasks run before `processResources`:

1. `svelteInstall` installs dependencies from your lockfile.
2. `svelteBuild` runs your build script.
3. `svelteBundle` copies the output to `ktor-svelte/public/` in your resources, and writes `ktor-svelte/manifest.json` with a hash of every file.

`svelteBundle` leaves out hidden files such as `.env` (but keeps `.well-known`), source maps and symlinks, and warns about any hidden files it skipped. `SvelteSource.Directory` also ignores hidden files and symlinks, but serves source maps. It streams each file through a non-blocking file channel with its exact `Content-Length`, which makes it a good fit for large builds served from a volume.

At run time, `install(Svelte)` adds a catch-all route. Ktor always prefers more specific routes, so yours win. GET and HEAD requests that reach the catch-all are resolved in this order:

| Step | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Path under an API prefix | Not handled, so Ktor returns its normal 404 |
| 2 | Exact file in the manifest | Serve the file |
| 3 | `/about` when `about.html` exists, or `/about/` when `about/index.html` exists | Serve the page |
| 4 | `/about/` when only `about.html` exists, or `/about` when only `about/index.html` exists | 308 redirect to the form that exists, keeping the query string |
| 5 | Missing path under `/_app/`, `/.well-known/` or `/_ktor-svelte/`, or any path with a file extension | 404, never the fallback |
| 6 | Other path, with a fallback page and a request that accepts HTML, or a path matching `paramRoutes` | Serve the fallback with status 200 |
| 7 | Anything else | `404.html` with status 404 if it exists, otherwise a plain 404 |

Because your routes always win, a Ktor `GET /about` hides a prerendered `about.html`. The app warns about every such route at startup, for example `ktor-svelte: the Ktor route GET /about hides the frontend page about.html.` Routes under your API prefixes and routes with parameters are not checked.

Step 4 exists because prerendered pages load assets with relative paths, so serving `about.html` at `/about/` would break them. Every file from the build answers `Range: bytes=...` requests with 206 and `Content-Range`, so videos can seek and downloads can resume. Ranges are always served without `Content-Encoding`, `If-Range` is honoured, and a range past the end of the file answers 416. Other methods on a path that resolves to a page or file, such as a POST to `/about`, answer 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`, and OPTIONS answers 204 with the same header. Paths that resolve to nothing stay 404. In development, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE still go to Vite first.

Step 5 lets SvelteKit recover from stale chunks after a deploy by doing a full page reload.

## Limits

- `adapter-static` only. There is no Node process in production, so `+page.server.ts`, `+server.ts` and form actions are not supported. Ktor is the backend. The [FAQ](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/faq) explains why and what to use instead.
- The app is mounted at the root. `paths.base` is not supported yet.
- Files are served whole or as one byte range. Requests for several ranges at once get the whole file. Very large media still makes the JAR large, so a CDN or object storage is often the better home for it.
- `generateTs` builds on Ktor's OpenAPI support, which Ktor still marks as experimental.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/architecture

# Architecture

How a SvelteKit build ends up in the JAR, and how a request reaches a file. Read this before changing the plugin or the runtime. [How it works](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/how-it-works) has the exact resolution rules.

## Build time

The Gradle plugin turns the frontend into resources of your app. Each step is a cacheable task, wired before `processResources`:

| Step | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `svelteInstall` | Installs dependencies from the lockfile with the detected package manager | `tasks/SvelteTasks.kt`, `PackageManager.kt` |
| `svelteBuild` | Runs the build script. Its inputs include a fingerprint of the package manager | `tasks/SvelteTasks.kt`, `tasks/ToolFingerprint.kt` |
| `svelteBundle` | Copies the output to `ktor-svelte/public/`, gzips what the adapter did not compress, hashes inline scripts and writes `ktor-svelte/manifest.json` | `tasks/SvelteBundleTask.kt`, `tasks/InlineScripts.kt` |
| `svelteSync` | Writes the frontend library setup and generated files from `svelte { libraries { } }` | `tasks/SvelteSyncTasks.kt`, `libraries/` |

Paths are relative to `ktor-svelte-gradle-plugin/src/main/kotlin/io/github/nijasc/ktor/svelte/gradle/`.

The manifest is the contract between the two halves. It lists every servable file with its size, hash, precompressed variants and, for HTML pages, the hashes of their inline scripts. The runtime never turns a request path into a file path. It only looks paths up in the manifest.

## Request time

`install(Svelte)` adds a catch-all route and a few hooks. Ktor prefers more specific routes, so your own routes always win.

| Step | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Guards | Origin check, body size, JSON shape limits and rate limits on API paths | `internal/security/RequestGuards.kt`, `JsonShapeLimits.kt`, `RateLimits.kt` |
| Catch-all | Takes GET and HEAD requests that no route of yours answered, and answers 405 for other methods on known pages | `internal/SvelteHandler.kt` |
| Resolution | Maps the path to a manifest entry, a 308 redirect, the SPA fallback or a 404 | `internal/assets/RequestResolver.kt` |
| Response | Sets `Cache-Control`, `ETag` and CSP, picks a precompressed variant, serves byte ranges and injects `publicConfig` | `internal/assets/AssetResponder.kt`, `ByteRanges.kt`, `ConfigInjector.kt` |
| Storage | Opens files from the classpath or from `SvelteSource.Directory` | `internal/assets/AssetStore.kt`, `Manifest.kt` |

Paths are relative to `ktor-svelte-server/src/main/kotlin/io/github/nijasc/ktor/svelte/`. The root package holds only the public API, such as `Svelte.kt` and `SvelteConfig.kt`.

## Development

In development mode the same catch-all sends frontend requests to Vite through `internal/dev/DevProxy.kt`, which uses the JDK `HttpClient` and only serves local clients. Your API routes still answer directly, so the browser talks to one origin.

`generateTs` reads Ktor's OpenAPI model of your routes when the app starts and writes the TypeScript client. That code lives in `internal/typescript/`, and the client templates are TypeScript files under `src/main/resources`. The development-only endpoints, such as the route table and the status page, are in `internal/dev/`.

`svelteDevAll` starts Vite and the app together, waits until both answer, and prints one ready banner. See `tasks/SvelteDevAllTask.kt` and `tasks/ReadyBanner.kt`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/troubleshooting

# Troubleshooting

Find the message you see, then its cause and fix. Run `./gradlew svelteDoctor` first: it checks the frontend setup and lists most problems on this page at once.

## Build

### ktor-svelte found no lockfile

The frontend has no `bun.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock`, so the plugin cannot tell which package manager to use. Install the dependencies once with your package manager, or set `svelte { packageManager = PackageManager.BUN }`.

### ktor-svelte could not find bun on PATH

The package manager the lockfile asks for is not installed, or Gradle cannot see it. Install it, restart the Gradle daemon with `./gradlew --stop` so it picks up the new `PATH`, or set `packageManager` to one you have. To have the plugin download Bun for you, set `svelte { bunVersion = "1.3.14" }`.

### ktor-svelte found no HTML files

The frontend build produced no pages where the plugin looked. Check that the frontend uses `adapter-static`, and that `svelte { outputDir }` matches the adapter's `pages` option. The default for both is `build`.

### ktor-svelte has no setting 'x' in svelte { }

A Groovy build script assigns a setting that does not exist, usually a typo. The message names the closest setting and lists all of them. See [Gradle settings](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/gradle) for what each one does.

### Frontend libraries are out of sync

`build.gradle.kts` changed the frontend libraries, but `package.json`, the lockfile or the generated files were not updated. Run `./gradlew svelteSync` and commit the result.

### ktor-svelte generates vite.config.ts, but found your own version

The plugin needs to own `vite.config.ts` and the hooks files once frontend libraries are on. Move your own Vite settings to `vite.user.ts`, merge custom hooks by hand, delete those files and run `svelteSync`.

### Generated TypeScript is out of date

`check` runs `svelteVerifyTs`, which found that a route or DTO changed but the committed client did not. Run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs`, or start the app in development mode, and commit the files in `frontend/src/lib/api`.

### The frontend build failed with exit code 1

ktor-svelte hides the package manager and Vite output while it succeeds and prints all of it when it fails, above this message. To see it every time, add `-Psvelte.verbose=true`.

## Startup

### ktor-svelte found no frontend build

The app runs in production mode, but the JAR has no frontend in it. Build it with the Gradle plugin and without `-Psvelte.skip=true` or `-Psvelte.dev=true`. During development, start it with `-Dio.ktor.development=true`, or use `svelteDevAll`, which does that for you.

### ktor-svelte manifest has format version 2, but this runtime reads version 1

The Gradle plugin and `ktor-svelte-server` have different versions. Use the same version for both. With `addRuntimeDependency` on, which is the default, the plugin adds the matching runtime for you.

### ContentNegotiation is already installed

You install `ContentNegotiation` yourself and also list formats in `transport { }`. Keep one of the two. The same applies to `Compression` and `compression()`.

### RequestBodyLimit is already installed, or RateLimit is already installed

ktor-svelte installs these plugins for its body and rate limits. To use your own, set `maxApiBodySize = null` or `rateLimit { enabled = false }`.

### ktor-svelte will not proxy to this URL because it is not on this machine

`dev { url }` or `KTOR_SVELTE_DEV_SERVER` points at another host. Use a loopback address, or set `dev { allowRemote = true }` if you trust that machine.

### Install the Svelte plugin before calling svelte() in routing

With `routing = SvelteRouting.Manual`, call `install(Svelte)` before the `routing { }` block that calls `svelte()`.

### The Ktor route GET /about hides the frontend page about.html

A route in your app answers the same path as a prerendered page, so the page is never served. Move the route under your API prefix, or rename the page.

## Requests

### 403: Cross-origin API request refused

The origin check refused a write from another site. If that site is yours, such as a separate admin frontend, add it with `allowedOrigins("https://admin.example.com")`. Behind a proxy that changes the host, install `XForwardedHeaders` so the app sees the host the browser used. See [Security](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards).

### 413: Request body is larger than the limit

API bodies are limited to 1 MiB. Raise `maxApiBodySize` for apps that accept uploads.

### 429: Too Many Requests

A client sent more than 120 writes to API paths in a minute, or hit a named limit. Behind a proxy, install `XForwardedHeaders`, or all users share one limit. Raise `rateLimit { apiWrites = ... }` if your app writes a lot.

### 503 in development: no Vite and no build

The app runs in development mode, Vite is not running and there is no frontend build. Start everything with `./gradlew svelteDevAll`, or Vite alone with `./gradlew svelteDev`.

### 403: The dev proxy only answers requests from this machine

You opened the app from another device while it runs in development mode. Set `dev { allowRemote = true }` on a network you trust.

### A page shows a blank screen after a deploy

The browser has an old page that loads chunks which no longer exist. ktor-svelte answers those with 404 on purpose, so SvelteKit reloads the page. If it does not, check that nothing in front of the app caches HTML: pages are sent with `Cache-Control: no-cache`.

## Development

### The browser logs a WebSocket error for HMR

Without `server.hmr.clientPort` in `vite.config.ts`, Vite's client first tries Ktor's port. Hot reload still works after one error. Projects from `svelteInit` already set it.

### A port is already in use

A Vite or app process from an earlier run is still alive, usually because a terminal was killed. Run `./gradlew --stop`, or stop the process on that port. `svelteDevAll` stops its children even when its terminal closes.

### Types do not update after a Kotlin change

The client is generated when the app starts in development mode with `generateTs = true`. With `svelteDevAll`, that happens after every Kotlin change. With separate terminals, restart the app, or run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs`.

## Still stuck?

Open an [issue](https://github.com/nijasc/ktor-svelte/issues) with the full message, your `install(Svelte)` and `svelte { }` blocks, and the output of `./gradlew svelteDoctor`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/faq

# FAQ

Questions people ask before and while using ktor-svelte.

**Why `adapter-static` and no server-side rendering?** ktor-svelte exists to ship one JVM app. SSR needs a JavaScript runtime that renders every request, so production would need Node next to the JVM, or a JavaScript engine inside it. That means two processes or a slow embedded engine, two places for auth and config, and two things to deploy and monitor. With `adapter-static`, the frontend is plain files, Ktor is the only backend, and the JAR is the whole app.

**What about SEO and the first paint?** Prerender every page whose content is known at build time with `export const prerender = true`. Those pages are real HTML that search engines and slow devices see right away. Pages that depend on data from your API render in the browser, which suits dashboards, admin areas and anything behind a login.

**How do I load data for a page?** Call your Ktor routes from `load` in `+page.ts` or from the component, through the generated client. `+page.server.ts` and `+server.ts` need a Node server and do not exist here. Write that logic as a Ktor route instead.

**What replaces form actions?** A Ktor route that receives the form as JSON or form data. Validation errors come back as a 422 that `isValidationError` understands, so the form can show them next to each field.

**Can I still add SSR later?** Yes, but not with ktor-svelte. Switch the frontend to `adapter-node`, run it as its own server, and keep Ktor as the API behind it. You lose the single JAR and the same-origin setup, and you need CORS or a proxy.

**Does a dynamic route like `/notes/[id]` work?** Yes. Unknown paths get the fallback page, and SvelteKit renders the route in the browser. List patterns in `paramRoutes` to serve the fallback for them even when a request does not accept HTML.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/compatibility

| Kotlin | 2.3 and newer | 2.4.21 |
| JVM | 17 and newer | 17, 21 |
| Gradle | Latest 8.x and 9.x | 8.14.6, 9.9.0 |
| SvelteKit | 3.x | 3.1.1 |
| Svelte | 5.57.3 and newer | 5.57.3 |
| Package managers | Bun, pnpm, npm, Yarn | Bun end to end. The others use fake tools in tests, plus npm in CI |

On Gradle 8.x, use Shadow 9.2 or older if you use Shadow. Newer versions need a newer Gradle.

# Upgrading

While the version starts with `0.`, a minor release such as 0.8.0 to 0.9.0 can change behaviour. Patch releases such as 0.9.0 to 0.9.1 only fix bugs. Each release that changes what your app does, or what you need to write, has a guide with the steps to adopt it. The [changelog](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/changelog) links each release to its guide.

To upgrade across several releases, follow the guides in order.

| Release | What changes for you |
|---|---|
| [0.11](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.11) | Generated Kotlin moves to `io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte`, and apps serve a generated `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` |
| [0.10](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.10) | `publicConfig` is inlined into pages, API responses carry a build header, and `svelteDevAll` opens the browser |
| [0.9](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.9) | Wrong methods on pages answer 405, JSON request bodies have a nesting limit, and every request gets an `X-Request-Id` |
| [0.8](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.8) | API responses of 1 KiB or more are compressed |
| [0.7](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.7) | API writes are rate limited per client |
| [0.6](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.6) | Security headers, a strict Content-Security-Policy, an origin check and a body size limit |

Releases before 0.6 only added features, so they need no steps.

## Bump the version

The Gradle plugin adds the matching runtime library for you, so one version change upgrades both:

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("io.github.nijasc.ktor-svelte") version "<new version>"
}
```

If you set `addRuntimeDependency = false` and declare `ktor-svelte-server` yourself, bump it to the same version. Then run `./gradlew svelteSync` once, because generated files and frontend library setup can change between releases.

Afterwards, `./gradlew svelteConfig` shows every setting with its new default and suggests what to turn on, so you notice new options. See [Review your configuration](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/reference/gradle#review-your-configuration).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.11

# Upgrading to 0.11

0.11 renames the package of generated Kotlin and adds two files to production apps. Most apps only need to update imports.

## Generated Kotlin moved to io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte

With frontend libraries on, ktor-svelte generates Kotlin such as `AppTheme`, `LucideIcon`, `Messages` and the `call.theme` and `call.messages` extensions. They now live in `io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte` instead of `ktorsvelte`, so they no longer sit in a top-level package of their own. Update your imports:

```kotlin
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.AppTheme
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.LucideIcon
import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.messages
```

In IntelliJ, replace `import ktorsvelte.` with `import io.github.nijasc.ktorsvelte.` across the project. To keep the old package instead, set it in `build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
svelte {
    libraries {
        generatedPackage = "ktorsvelte"
    }
}
```

## sitemap.xml and robots.txt

When your build has no `sitemap.xml` or `robots.txt`, ktor-svelte now serves generated ones: a sitemap of your prerendered pages, and a `robots.txt` that keeps crawlers out of your API. Set `siteUrl` to your public address, put your own files in `frontend/static/`, or turn both off with `sitemap = false`. See [Sitemap and robots.txt](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/endpoints#sitemap-and-robots-txt).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.10

# Upgrading to 0.10

0.10 adds features that change a few responses and the dev loop. Most apps need no changes.

## publicConfig is inlined into pages

When you set `publicConfig`, every page from your build now contains it as `<script type="application/json" id="ktor-svelte-config">`, and pages get their own ETag. The generated `loadPublicConfig()` reads it from there before asking the server.

You are affected only if a test compares page bodies byte for byte, or a cache in front of the app keys on the build hash. Set `inlinePublicConfig = false` to keep pages unchanged. See [Runtime config](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/runtime-config).

## Build header on API responses

API responses now carry `X-Ktor-Svelte-Build` with a short fingerprint of the frontend build, so the generated client can tell when a new version is deployed. Set `buildHeader = false` to leave it out.

## svelteDevAll opens the browser

`svelteDevAll` opens the app in your default browser once, when it is first ready. It never does in CI or without a display. Turn it off in `build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
svelte {
    dev {
        openBrowser = false
    }
}
```

## Paths under /_ktor-svelte/

Unknown paths under `/_ktor-svelte/` now answer 404 instead of the SPA fallback, because ktor-svelte reserves them for its own endpoints. If your SvelteKit app has a route there, move it.

## Regenerate the client

The generated client gained timeouts, `latest()`, `onNewBuild`, JSDoc from route descriptions and companions for sealed class unions. Start the app once in development, or run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs`, and commit the updated files under `src/lib/api`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.9

# Upgrading to 0.9

0.9 changes three responses. Most apps need no changes.

## 405 for wrong methods on pages

A POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE to a path that is a page or file of your build, such as `/about`, now answers 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`, instead of 404. OPTIONS answers 204. Paths that resolve to nothing still answer 404.

You are affected if a test or monitor expects 404 for such a request. Update the expected status.

## JSON nesting limit

JSON request bodies on API paths that nest deeper than 64 levels now answer 400. Real payloads rarely nest beyond 10.

If you accept deeply nested documents, raise the limit, or turn it off with `null`:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    maxJsonDepth = 256
}
```

`maxJsonStringLength` can also refuse long strings. It is off by default. See [JSON shape](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards).

## Request IDs

Every request now gets an `X-Request-Id` response header, and the generated client sends one with each call. Unhandled errors are logged with the ID, and `ApiError.requestId` carries it in the frontend.

You are affected only if you install Ktor's `CallId` yourself. ktor-svelte then uses your setup and does not install its own. To turn the feature off, set `requestIds = false`.

## Regenerate the client

The generated client now sends request IDs. Start the app once in development, or run `./gradlew svelteGenerateTs`, and commit the updated files under `src/lib/api`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.8

# Upgrading to 0.8

0.8 compresses API responses of 1 KiB or more with gzip or deflate, and with zstd when its Ktor module is on the classpath.

## Apps that install Ktor's Compression themselves

Nothing changes. When `Compression` is already installed, ktor-svelte leaves it alone and uses your configuration. To let ktor-svelte handle API paths instead, remove your installation.

To keep API responses uncompressed, turn it off:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    apiCompression = false
}
```

## Endpoints that return secrets

A response that mixes a secret, such as an API key, with text an attacker can choose can leak the secret through its compressed size. If you have such an endpoint, turn `apiCompression` off, or install `Compression` yourself with a condition that skips that route. See [API compression](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/transport#api-compression).

## Proxies and tests

Clients that send `Accept-Encoding` now get a compressed body with `Content-Encoding`. Browsers and Ktor's client handle this on their own. Tests that read raw bytes, or proxies that rewrite bodies, may need to decompress first or send no `Accept-Encoding`.

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.7

# Upgrading to 0.7

0.7 rate limits writes to your API by default. Each client may send 120 requests per minute with any method except GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE. More answer 429 with `Retry-After`.

## Behind a reverse proxy

Clients are told apart by `call.request.origin.remoteHost`. Without forwarded headers, every request seems to come from the proxy, so all users share one budget. Install Ktor's `XForwardedHeaders` or `ForwardedHeaders` before upgrading.

## Apps with heavy write traffic

Raise the default, or turn it off for one deployment:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    rateLimit {
        apiWrites = 600
    }
}
```

`rateLimit { enabled = false }` turns it off completely.

## Apps that install Ktor's RateLimit themselves

ktor-svelte now installs Ktor's `RateLimit` plugin, and Ktor allows it only once. Move your limits into `rateLimit { limit(...) }` and keep wrapping routes with `rateLimit(RateLimitName("..."))`:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    rateLimit {
        limit("login", requests = 5, per = 1.minutes)
    }
}

routing {
    rateLimit(RateLimitName("login")) {
        post("/api/login") { /* ... */ }
    }
}
```

Or set `rateLimit { enabled = false }` and keep your own installation.

## Tests

Tests that send many writes in a row can now get 429. Raise `apiWrites` in the test setup, or turn the limit off there. See [Rate limit](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#api-request-guards).

Source: https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/migrations/0.6

# Upgrading to 0.6

0.6 turns on four protections by default. Most apps need no changes. Check each section that applies to you.

## Security headers and CSP

Every response now gets `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `Referrer-Policy`, and every page from your build gets a strict `Content-Security-Policy` built from its own inline scripts.

You are affected if your pages load scripts, images, fonts or API calls from another origin, such as analytics or a CDN, or if another site embeds your app in a frame. The browser console shows each blocked request.

Allow what you need:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    securityHeaders {
        allowCspSources("script-src", "https://plausible.io")
        allowCspSources("connect-src", "https://plausible.io")
        frameOptions = "SAMEORIGIN"
    }
}
```

`automaticContentSecurityPolicy = false` drops the CSP and keeps the other headers. See [Security headers](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/security#security-headers).

## Origin check

Writes to API paths, meaning every method except GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE, from a browser on another site now answer 403.

You are affected if a frontend on another origin, such as a separate admin app, calls your API. List it:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    allowedOrigins("https://admin.example.com")
}
```

Behind a reverse proxy that changes the `Host` header, install Ktor's `XForwardedHeaders` or `ForwardedHeaders`, so the check compares against the public host. Server-to-server calls and tests without an `Origin` header are not affected.

## Body size limit

Request bodies on API paths larger than 1 MiB now answer 413.

You are affected if you accept uploads or large imports. Raise the limit, or remove it with `null`:

```kotlin
install(Svelte) {
    maxApiBodySize = 50L * 1024 * 1024
}
```

If you installed Ktor's `RequestBodyLimit` yourself, keep it only with `maxApiBodySize = null`, because both cannot be installed together.

## Generated validation

The generated client now has a `validate()` per request type, built from your schema constraints. Nothing changes for existing calls. See [Validation](https://nijasc.github.io/ktor-svelte/main/features/validation) to use it in forms.
